item.title: Fisherman Sets Lake Record at Fort Phantom Hill
item.description: ABILENE, TX — Abilene’s Travis McCollough reeled in a 14.35-pound largemouth bass at Fort Phantom Hill Reservoir on Feb. 5, setting a new waterbody record at the lake just north of Abilene.McCollough’s catch was a Legacy Class ShareLunker, a distinction reserved for fish weighing 13 pounds or more. Four Legacy Class ShareLunkers have been caught in Texas so far this year, with the others coming from Toledo Bend, O.H. Ivie and Alan Henry. Learn More Here.

item.title: Mason’s Whitworth Hits Milestone With 2,000 Career Points
item.description: MASON, TX — Mason’s Anna Marie Whitworth hit an impressive milestone recently with her 2,000th career point for the Cowgirls basketball team.Whitworth, a 6-foot-2 power forward, has led the Cowgirls to a 35-1 record and the No. 2 ranking in the state in Class 2A. Learn More Here.

item.title: San Angelo Water: Online Card Payments Restored Temporarily
item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — The City of San Angelo has restored online credit and debit card payments for water utility bills using a temporary third-party processor, city officials announced Feb. 13. Learn More Here.

item.title: 2 Central High School Students Named All-State in Band, Choir
item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — Central High School has two students who have reached the top level a high school musician can achieve through the Texas Music Educators Association by earning all-state honors in band and choir. Junior Ian Caraballo-Pagan, who plays the clarinet, was named to the 6A All-State Symphonic Band for the second time. Learn More Here.

item.title: UPDATE: San Angelo Police Identify Suspect in Junius Street Shooting
item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — The San Angelo Police Department identified the suspect in a shooting that took place on Junius Street on Friday, Feb. 13.Marcus Parker, 41, is being charged with felon in possession of a firearm, and additional charges are pending, according to Police Chief Travis Griffith. Learn More Here.

item.title: LIVE! Daily News | Chief Griffith Updates San Angelo on Violent Crimes

item.title: Vehicle Crash Downs Utility Pole, Causes Outage in San Angelo
item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — A motor vehicle crash near the intersection of Glenna and Junius streets knocked down a utility pole and triggered a power outage affecting 49 customers Friday evening. The San Angelo Police Department issued a public alert shortly after 5 p.m. advising motorists to avoid the area near the soccer fields. AEP Texas reported the outage began at 5:15 p.m. Feb. 13, with restoration estimated by 9:30 p.m. Learn More Here.

item.title: Central Downs Mojo in OT, Claims Guaranteed Share of the District Title
item.description: ODESSA, TX — It would not be a District 2-6A rivalry without some late-game action and drama, and in the matchup between the Central Bobcats and Permian Panthers in Odessa on Friday night, there was plenty of both. Central led Mojo down to the wire before it took an overtime period to finally decide a winner. The Bobcats emerged victorious and claimed a guaranteed share of the District 2-6A Championship, 67-61. Learn More Here.

item.title: Failure to Report Sexual Assault, Organized Criminal Activity, and Drug Dealing Lead Bookings
Marginal Severe Thunderstorm Risk for San Angelo Area Today
item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — West-central Texas, including San Angelo, faces a marginal risk of severe thunderstorms Saturday, with the strongest storms capable of producing large hail up to 1 inch in diameter, gusty winds of 50 to 60 mph, frequent lightning, and brief heavy rainfall. The National Weather Service in San Angelo issued the outlook early Saturday, forecasting numerous thunderstorms across the region from early morning through late afternoon. Learn More Here.
